record.title: Anthropic researcher reports Claude-assisted full-sky ultraviolet map with prediction provenance
record.summary: Johns Hopkins astrophysicist and Anthropic researcher Brice Ménard reports using Claude Science and coordinated agents to harmonize ultraviolet observations from GALEX, Swift-UVOT, FIMS/SPEAR and TD-1, add Gaia-derived stellar estimates, and create an all-sky map. The author-hosted technical page says remaining gaps are filled by statistical regression and labels each pixel by provenance; it reports typical held-out errors of about 0.05–0.06 dex for predicted diffuse sky. Roughly one quarter to one third of the sky remains model-predicted depending on band and provenance layer, and the paper is marked in preparation. These are author-reported results; the downloadable data and code are not yet available on the page.
organizations: Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Ménard reports that Claude Science coordinated agents to harmonize multiple public UV surveys and produce a full-sky, two-band UV map with measured and predicted pixels explicitly labelled.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The author-hosted technical page reports spatially held-out typical errors around 0.05–0.06 dex for predicted diffuse sky, with error increasing farther from measurements and substantial band/regime-specific limitations.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Predicted regions are estimates rather than measured UV observations and cannot establish new sources or serve as an independent dust tracer.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The author reports that two rounds of agent review missed visible GALEX tile-footprint artifacts; human inspection identified them and Claude corrected per-tile residual backgrounds.

evidence_gaps.description: The technical paper and FITS/HiPS products are not yet downloadable from the author-hosted page, so the validation split, mask construction, calibration and map layers could not be independently inspected.
The map author reports that two rounds of agent review failed to notice tile-shaped calibration artifacts; the corrective process was also part of the same researcher/model workflow.
No time/cost accounting or comparison with a conventional human/automated pipeline was inspected, so the degree to which agents reduced scientific labor is unknown.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported map and validation hold, a unified UV sky reference with per-pixel measurement provenance could make legacy multi-mission observations substantially more usable and illustrates a meaningful agent-assisted science workflow. This is a single researcher-guided case, the technical paper remains in preparation, and independent review and downloadable artifacts are absent, limiting its consequence to meaningful rather than field-shaping.
limitations: All quantitative map and validation claims are first-party reports by the map author; the research desk did not reproduce them.
The technical paper is in preparation and downloadable map/code products were not available at inspection time.
Predicted regions are not measured and cannot be used to discover new sources or as independent dust tracers; resolution and uncertainty vary by provenance layer.
The author reports that two agent review rounds missed visible tile-disc artifacts, later corrected after human inspection, demonstrating residual QA dependence.
No matched baseline or agent-versus-human time/cost comparison was inspected.
organizations: Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute
brief.summary: Johns Hopkins astrophysicist and Anthropic researcher Brice Ménard reports using Claude Science and coordinated agents to harmonize ultraviolet observations from GALEX, Swift-UVOT, FIMS/SPEAR and TD-1, add Gaia-derived stellar estimates, and create an all-sky map. The author-hosted technical page says remaining gaps are filled by statistical regression and labels each pixel by provenance; it reports typical held-out errors of about 0.05–0.06 dex for predicted diffuse sky. Roughly one quarter to one third of the sky remains model-predicted depending on band and provenance layer, and the paper is marked in preparation. These are author-reported results; the downloadable data and code are not yet available on the page.

technical.claimed_result: A first detailed all-sky map in far-UV and near-UV combining measured surveys with provenance-labelled model estimates; about 28% far-UV and 27% near-UV is predicted by the detailed page, with held-out prediction scatter reported around 0.047/0.057 dex in selected regimes.
technical.demonstrated_result: The public pages and interactive map exist and document the authors’ workflow and product. the research desk inspected the text and interactive product description but did not download or independently validate the map, code, photometry or holdout analysis.
technical.mechanism: The reported workflow cleans and jointly re-levels about 38,000 GALEX tiles, cross-calibrates Swift-UVOT, FIMS/SPEAR and TD-1 data, predicts remaining diffuse UV from multi-wavelength tracers using gradient-boosted decision trees, adds Gaia stellar flux estimates, and publishes per-pixel provenance weights and uncertainty layers. The technical page distinguishes this statistical regression from a language model or image generator; Claude is described as orchestrating data collection, coding and processing agents.
technical.novelty: The contribution is an agent-assisted, multi-survey data harmonization and completion workflow with explicit measured-versus-predicted provenance and uncertainty, not a new astronomical observation or discovery.
technical.regime: Astronomical diffuse UV background and stellar flux across the full sky, combining legacy GALEX GR6/7 with Swift-UVOT, FIMS/SPEAR, TD-1, Planck, H-alpha/H I tracers and Gaia DR3. Predicted pixels have lower effective spatial resolution (roughly 0.5–1 degree or degree scale in some FIMS-constrained far-UV regions).
technical.reproducibility: Technical paper is listed as in preparation; linked downloads are not yet available. No code or data were downloaded or executed and no independent astronomy review was found in this check.
technical.strongest_baseline: The technical page compares held-out predictions against known GALEX observations hidden in spatial patches and reports independent-survey agreement where available; it does not establish a matched external pipeline comparison in the reviewed material.

brief.title: Anthropic researcher reports Claude-assisted full-sky ultraviolet map with prediction provenance
brief.why_it_matters: The reported workflow turns heterogeneous, partly missing astronomical surveys into a unified, uncertainty-labelled reference product and is a concrete case of agent-supported scientific data engineering. Its value depends on whether the calibration and spatial holdout results survive independent domain review. Predicted sky is an estimate from correlated tracers, not a new observation, and cannot support discovery of new sources in those regions.
